Projection chapter

Orthogonal Projections: quality and coverage audit

Edition: 15October2026. Status: completed author review draft, subject to student approval. The entire existing library is not claimed to have been revised by this delivery.

Instruction and problems

The chapter has25 numbered teaching sections,50 separately worked mathematical/conceptual problems, two explicitly repeated authentic examination placements, a complete summary and50 complete final decisions. The first ten independently written problems were retained and integrated with forty further derivations. Four problem entries reconstruct the entire MIT exercise16.1–16.6 family, grouping the three closely related residual/reprojection exercises in one explained problem. A Berkeley numerical example is independently explained and checked. Course-derived work is identified; invented problems are not presented as authentic examinations. Difficulty varies from prerequisite checks through medium and hard synthesis; an author difficulty judgment is not empirical calibration against candidate performance.

All lesson proofs, problem statements, answers and final decisions were read through during authoring. The emphasis is the chain of reasoning: declared metric and dimensions, feasible membership, perpendicular residual, uniqueness and an independent energy/distance certificate. Important extensions include dependent coordinates, weighted and complex geometry, affine feasibility, trace and diagonal constraints, oblique counterexamples, reflections, coordinate changes, finite alternating projections and conditioning. Later detailed least-squares estimation and SVD theory remain separate scheduled chapters.

Sources and original examinations

The chapter-specific source audit compares a bounded seven-university pool and selects MIT, Stanford, Berkeley and Oxford as four complementary core courses. Exact reading ranges, faculty and written references are recorded. Oxford contributes metric/adjoint foundations rather than pretending to contain every projection theorem. ETH provides additional historically reviewed QR support. CMU and Harvard are documented evaluated candidates. The audit separates previous reading from the fresh MIT/Stanford text, Oxford pages and four Berkeley original images inspected on15October.

The original MSc CS1405 question41 and PhD CS1404 question31 PDFs were rendered and visually checked again, including the option order. Both file hashes match the recorded original archive provenance. The chapter labels their reuse and independently derived answers. The MSc question is extended to a Frobenius closest-point construction without mislabeling the added derivation as part of the original examination.

Mathematical and document checks

The dedicated verification reports1752 successful assertions in l_projection-evidence/mathematics.json, in addition to the retained first-ten bank oracle. It checks all further numbered problem calculations or counterexamples, a bounded exact rational family of projector-pair identities, all1046 native MathML expressions for balanced fences and valid scripted bases, and the actual JavaScript stored model certificates. The centering examples use dimensions1through8, not an assertion that every dimension was enumerated; the general formula is proved in the text. Exact example checks support but do not replace the written proofs.

Visuals and behavior

Thirteen compact interactive placements contain73 finite checkpoints. They separately depict real two-dimensional projections, weighted coordinate geometry, affine constraints, reflection, oblique range/kernel behavior, alternating finite products and a three-dimensional plane view. Two original static vector figures distinguish coefficient-space nonuniqueness and a function-space residual. The diagrams do not draw a Euclidean right-angle mark for weighted geometry or claim that a screen angle in a three-dimensional view is the physical angle.

The owned browser review checks the real fonts, all model checkpoints, text bounds and padding, marker references, previous/next/restart/seek controls for all thirteen placements, actual timer playback on five representative players, editable ordinary/weighted/end-angle examples, invalid-input preservation, widths390/768/1360, absence of underlined links, single-row display formulas and printed answer/keyframe availability. The final evidence and screenshots are in l_projection-evidence/browser.json. The screen layout keeps the figures compact; narrow screens scroll the illustration internally instead of expanding the page. Small finite-iterate segments are drawn without an oversized arrowhead when too short for one.

Explicit limits

No finite audit establishes literal100percent correctness, exhausts every worldwide course or guarantees perfect performance on every unseen question. These are complete current review drafts with stated scope, not externally peer-reviewed textbooks or student-approved editions. The browser checks cover the recorded devices/widths and representative playback, not every browser or every possible real-number input. Model decimals are rounded and labeled. The complete Site update remains publication-pending while the official source connection resets; offline copies and the verified GitHub mirror are separately tracked rather than confused with a successful Site deployment.
